recipes.name: Maple Glazed Chicken with Sweet Potatoes
ingredients_raw: 1.5 pounds sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces
2 teaspoons steak seasoning (such as Montreal Steak Seasoning®)

steps.text: Place the sweet potatoes into a large pot and cover with water. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until tender, about 20 minutes. Drain and allow to steam dry for a minute or two. Mash the potatoes, and set aside.

Sprinkle chicken tenders with steak seasoning; heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat, and cook the chicken tenders until the meat is lightly browned and no longer pink inside, 5 to 8 minutes per side. Remove the chicken, and set aside. Stir the maple syrup into the skillet, scraping up and dissolving any browned flavor bits from the skillet. Bring to a boil, simmer for 2 minutes, and stir in the green onions.
To serve, place the mashed sweet potatoes onto a serving platter, top with the chicken tenders, and pour the maple sauce over the chicken.

raw_recipe.headline: Maple Glazed Chicken with Sweet Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: Pan-fried chicken tenders are served with mashed sweet potatoes and an easy maple syrup sauce with green onions in this weeknight-friendly supper.

review.reviewBody:
Well, I didn't have any chicken so I used hamburger, and I didn't have any sweet potatoes so I used turnips, and I didn't have maple syrup so I used molasses, but I still feel I am justified in reviewing this recipe....no, no, none of the above is true, it's just that some of the reviews on this site can be so annoying sometimes. 

Anyways, this recipe actually is lovely! Fast, easy, and it tastes great! 5 stars.

This was SO GOOD! I made it quite a bit differently though, but I think I got a pretty similar result. I oven roasted the potatoes (flesh side down on parchment paper, 400° for 50 minutes.) I sauteed chicken breast after seasoning with salt, pepper, steak seasoning, and a dash of chili powder. Once I removed the chicken breast from the pan, I directly put a bunch of shoelace cut red onion on the pan until it was completely sauteed and soaked up all that yummy chicken seasoning. I added 1/3 cup of SUGAR FREE syrup and constantly stirred for about 1 minute. It started to blacken quickly so I took it right off and put the onions on top of the chicken bowl. I added some peas for a little extra mmph. Starting from the bottom of the bowl it was 1/2 a mashed sweet potato, 4 oz chicken, 1/3 cup of peas, small pile of sweet syrupy red onion. It was SO. STINKING. GOOD!

The BF liked this quite a bit. I baked the potato instead, so during that time I marinated the cut up boneless, skinless chicken thighs (he likes those better than breasts) in the steak seasoning. Mashed the potato with a bit of butter. After I browned the chicken and removed them from the pan (I was another that used red onion vs the green) I caramelized the red onion...I only had a sugar-free syrup but suppose that's okay. I did use the chopped green onion on top and that really made for a pretty dish.

I already had roasted sweet potatoes and honeynut squash from my garden (like butternut squash but sweeter) that were leftover from a previous dinner so I reheated them and then whipped them up with some extra Amish butter while cooking the chicken. I also used a good amount of Montreal Steak Seasoning to season the chicken and cooked the chicken in the Amish butter rather than oil. I used Wood’s Vermont smoked maple syrup for the real maple syrup which is incredible and sliced up about a cup of green onions I wanted to finish up. This dish was so good that my husband even went back for seconds. And he’s really more of a beef man since we raise our own.

Bomb Diggity Dog!!! Wife and I Devoured the whole thing! Tweeked it a bit but stayed the course.. only extras I did were.... sautéed some red onions in the same pan as the chicken, throwing them in when chicken was half done, and removed all from the cast iron when chicken was done. Made the sauce as discribed but used a lil less than 1/2 cup of green onions..looked as if there would be more onions than sauce if I added it all. 
Added a 3tbs of butter, 1tbs brown sugar, and 1tbs of shredded coconut to the sweet potatoes before mashing, and used real maple syrup.. other than that I had to fight the wife off my plate.. Will definitely make again

I used chicken breasts butterflied and cut into strips. I also left out the onion and added chopped (cooked) bacon. Then I layered it into a baking pan and popped it into the oven for 10 minutes. So yummy!

This was a pretty yummy meal! I did add butter and brown sugar to the potatoes, just because I like it that way. I added pats of butter on top of the chicken towards the end of the sauteing, and cut the syrup to 1/4 cup. I pan fried some onions and shallots to top it off, that made all the difference! I would definitely recommend this dish, and I will make it again! Thanks

I was skeptical at first but who doesn't like a maple I used chicken thighs instead of tenders for the recipe and followed the rest. I prepared the chicken as directed and baked them for 30 mins and fried them for an additional 3-4 mins each side. It was delicious I will be making this again!

Just based on what I had on hand; I used chicken drumsticks, threw them in the slowcooker, added a bunch of chopped green onions, salt free veggie spice, drizzled a little olive oil and some maple syrup over top and walked away. Made up some sweet potatoes to go with it and the toddlers devoured it all caveman-style. So good, fall off the bone tender and surprisingly delicious.

Excellent and easy. I did not make the sweet potato component, I served the maple chicken and onion with coleslaw and potato salad. The maple chicken was moist, tender, and very easy to make. I had thick breasts, cooked them 6 minutes per side and then 2 more minutes with the onions and maple syrup in the fry pan.

I used the air fryer for the chicken tenders- cooked from frozen/ rubbed a little avocado oil on them and seasoned with steak seasoning- air fryed on 400 for 15 minutes turning once. Washed, poked and put a sweet potato in the microwave for 6 minutes. Cut up a bunch of green onions; once potato was cooked I put the onions on it, poured some 100% pure maple syrup on it and then topped it with the chicken. Fast healthy and yum!
Only had chicken legs which everyone enjoyed. (I think the tenders would have been better.)
Didn't use green onions. But will make it again.
My family loved this meal. It has been added to our make again list!! Only thing I added was a half stick of butter to the sweet potatoes!!!
This was so easy to make with a few ingredients, but it tasted so good! I loved the sweet and savory flavors. I will make this again.

My husband and I loved it. The syrup mixture gave it a wonderful flavor. I did add a couple of tablespoons of unsalted butter to the sweet potatoes but that is the only thing I changed. I used regular yellow onions it’s all I had. It probably didn’t need the butter. Delicious and filling.
So easy and good-better than boxed meals with an even easier recipe!
Easy,delicious did put butter in sweet potatoes but that's all! will make again!

I used red onion and burger seasoning because that's what I had on hand. I added a little butter to the sweet potatoes and threw some bacon into the syrup as I simmered the onions. The smell in the kitchen is lovely! The meal was great and so easy! Thank you!
The recipe calls for green onions but the picture is clearly using red onions, when and how is it prepared, using the onions.
